record_type_quote:
Fausey and Boroditsky (2010) demonstrated that agentive descriptions of accidents can
increase perceived blame and financial liability. We conducted direct replications of their
studies 1 and 2 in English, as originally used, and in Croatian.

targets.title: Subtle linguistic cues influence perceived blame and financial liability.
targets.evidence_quote:
Fausey and Boroditsky (2010) demonstrated that agentive descriptions of accidents can
increase perceived blame and financial liability. We conducted direct replications of their
studies 1 and 2 in English, as originally used, and in Croatian.
targets.outcome_quote:
We successfully replicated original findings in English, but results of the experiments
conducted in Croatian were mixed. In the first experiment, we found a smaller effect of
agentive language and only on the blame level and not on the proposed financial penalty. In
the second experiment, we did not find the effect of agentive language on the proposed fine.
targets.outcome_reasoning: English studies replicate; Croatian studies partly fail, explicitly framed as mixed. Aggregate all attempts against this one original.

reasoning: Identity and all three authors verified on Stage 2 manuscript. Re-tests published findings in fresh US and Croatian samples; related memory papers are background.
